video_directives: Tighten the 0-4s static volcano hook: add faster smoke/ember build or earlier title reveal to avoid a quiet open.
Keep character micro-reactions (X-eyes, ear-cover, sad slump) landing exactly on the beat they illustrate — this is working, protect it.
The 4-7s hold is one beat too long on the pointing pose; trim ~0.5s or add a subtle idle loop before the gauge cut.

top3_directives: Brighten the volcano glow and smoke plume — the mid-frame focal point is slightly muddy against the purple gradient, weakening the instant focal pull
Give the bottom wave/foreground band a touch more tonal separation from the title panel so the text plate doesn't read as a flat cut-out block
The crescent moon and orbit arcs are so faint they add nothing — either strengthen them into the composition or remove to clean the upper dead zone
The character in the lower-left is under-lit relative to the scene — raise its rim glow/exposure so it reads instantly on a daylight phone
Top third of the frame (starfield) is a near-dead zone — extend the eruption glow ring or ash plume upward to fill it
JAVA/SUMATRA labels sit on the horizon line in dim white; add subtle drop shadows or 10-15% size bump for daylight legibility
Add a subtle glow or rim light behind the cream text so it separates from the faint horizontal line artifacts crossing the letters
Fill the empty bottom quarter with a ground reflection or ash particles so the lower dead zone doesn't read as cropped
Tighten the character's pointing gesture so the arm clearly aims at the headline instead of floating between it and the volcano

Move the dead bottom-right third to life: the character is bottom-left and the pressure rings are faint — darken/tighten rings or shift the character composition so the lower half has a clear secondary focal point
Increase label contrast on the gauge: the '0' and '200' tick text sits low-contrast against the navy dial and will wash out on a daylight phone screen
Unify the caption pill with the gauge tip highlight — the orange glow on the needle and the orange accent in the pill are close but not identical; match hues for one cohesive accent system
Fix the hard horizontal seam between the purple gradient and the flat navy bottom band — blend it or design a deliberate divider so the two scenes don't read as a compositional accident
The sound-wave element entering the ear canal is too small and low-contrast (faint blue on purple) — enlarge it and add glow so the ear→sound relationship reads instantly
The bottom-right two-thirds is a dead zone with a tiny character in the far corner — scale the wincing figure up ~1.5x and center-right it, or add subtle wave/light details to occupy the void
Enlarge 'EARDRUMS SPLIT' ~1.5x and add subtle glow/outline so the secondary line survives daylight viewing at 6 inches
Rebalance the composition: character is pinned small in bottom-left leaving a large dead lower-right water zone — either scale the character up or shift it right toward the third
Unify the two text treatments into one system (same size/weight family) or add a slight drop shadow to the pill badge so it doesn't float ambiguously over the sky
Fill the top ~40% dead zone: the purple sky carries no subject or guide element — raise the explosion rings or add a smoke/star detail to compress the composition
The right-mid palm silhouettes and floating debris cluster reads as mush — either silhouette them darker against the glow or remove the ambiguous specks entirely
The '3,000 MILES AWAY' caption floats awkwardly mid-frame, straddling the horizon line — lock it to a consistent margin with the character or center it as a deliberate subtitle bar
Lift the character in the bottom band — its cream face and navy hoodie sink into the dark ground; add a rim light or local glow so it reads as a secondary subject rather than a smudge
The bottom-right quarter is a large dead zone — either extend the ground gradient/purple haze or nudge the caption chip and character into a tighter composition
Give the orbit ring a subtle luminance gradient so the satellite's glow has a directional source; currently the cyan dot reads as a floating sticker
Move the caption block lower into the dark mid-band or add a stronger scrim — white text over white wave foam kills edge contrast on a 6-inch daylight screen
Fill or crop the dead upper 40%: the empty purple sky with a tiny moon reads as a dead zone on vertical — push the wave/moon composition up or add subtle cloud/atmosphere layering
Unify the two text plates into one system — the stat pill and caption bar sit at slightly different widths and opacities, creating competing anchor points mid-frame
Move the glowing 'GONE.' text off the mountain peak where the hot lava glow fights its edge contrast — place it in clear sky space or add a stronger dark drop shadow
The bottom-right water quadrant is a large dead zone; either add subtle ripple/star reflections or reposition the circle vignette to balance mass
The gold circle crops awkwardly at both frame edges while the character overlaps it inconsistently — commit to it as a full deliberate frame device or reduce its opacity
Fill the top-third dead zone (empty starfield) — either raise the volcano higher or add subtle smoke/ash particles rising from the summit to connect summit glow to the sky
Character's pointing gesture leads the eye off-frame left; rotate the pose so the arm gestures toward the volcano/text to unify the eye path

Sub-caption chip ('CHILD OF KRAKATAU') is noticeably smaller and darker than the title — increase its text size ~20% or brighten the chip fill so both lines read at arm's length on a 6-inch phone in daylight
Bottom third is a large near-black dead zone — lift the water with subtle reflections of the lava glow or rim-light ripples toward the character
Character occludes the left base of the volcano awkwardly — shift subject right ~15% so the silhouette reads fully and eye path flows volcano→character
Add a faint warm bounce light on the character's front from the eruption to tie subject and focal point into one lighting story
